subject: maths
title: Short Division: the Bus Stop Method
seo_title: Year 5 Short Division Worksheets: Bus Stop Method, Remainders and Word Problems
standard_text: Divide numbers up to 4 digits by a one-digit number using the formal written method of short division and interpret remainders appropriately for the context.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on short division (the bus stop method): 2-, 3- and 4-digit numbers ÷ 1-digit numbers, zeros in the answer, remainders, rounding up or down in context, and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Divide one digit at a time from the left. Carry any remainder to the next digit.
key_sub: 4,028 ÷ 4 = 1,007: when the divisor does not go into a digit, write 0 in the answer. A remainder is always less than the divisor. In word problems, decide: round up, round down, or write the remainder as a fraction.
body_html:
The big idea

Short division shares a number into equal groups, one digit at a time, from the left. Write the number under the “bus stop” and the divisor outside. Divide each digit. If there is a remainder, carry it: write it as a small digit in front of the next digit.

Worked examples

Check with the inverse

957 ÷ 4 = 239 r 1. Is it right?

Multiply the answer by the divisor, then add the remainder: 239 × 4 = 956 and 956 + 1 = 957.

Answer: Yes, it is right

If the first digit is smaller than the divisor, carry it straight away: for 296 ÷ 8, 8 does not go into 2, so divide 29 next. The answer has one digit fewer: 37.

Remainders: what does the question want?

The question asksDo this61 children, 8 in each minibus: 61 ÷ 8 = 7 r 5
How many are needed for everyone?Round up8 minibuses
How many full groups?Round down7 full minibuses
How many are left over?The remainder is the answer5 children

When the thing can be split, such as a pizza, a cake or a length, write the remainder as a fraction: the remainder over the divisor. 23 pizzas ÷ 4 = 5 r 3 = 5 34 pizzas each.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Missing a zero (4,028 ÷ 4 = 107)When the divisor does not go into a digit, write 0 in the answer: 1,007
Not carrying the remainder (72 ÷ 4 = 10)7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3. Carry the 3 to make 32: the answer is 18
A remainder bigger than the divisor (238 r 5 for ÷ 4)The divisor goes in once more: 239 r 1
Rounding the wrong way (7 minibuses for 61 children)Ask: does everyone need a place? Then round up

faq.q: What is the bus stop method of division?
faq.a: It is the everyday name for short division. The number goes under a line shaped like a bus stop, the divisor sits outside, and you divide one digit at a time, carrying any remainder to the next digit.

faq.q: How do you teach short division in Year 5?
faq.a: Start with 2-digit and 3-digit numbers with no remainder, then add remainders and 4-digit numbers. Ask children to check every answer by multiplying, and to say what the remainder means in a word problem.

faq.q: What division should a Year 5 child know?
faq.a: Year 5 children divide numbers up to 4 digits by a one-digit number using short division. They also decide whether to round a remainder up or down, or write it as a fraction, depending on the question.

faq.q: How do you explain a remainder to a child?
faq.a: A remainder is what is left over when a number cannot be shared equally. It is always smaller than the number you divide by; if it is not, the divisor goes in once more.

sets.title: Short division with no remainder: 2-digit and 3-digit numbers

items.q: Mohammed uses short division for 743 ÷ 4. First, 7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3. What does he divide next?
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3. The remainder 3 is 3 hundreds, which is 30 tens. Write it as a small 3 in front of the 4, so you divide 34 next: 34 ÷ 4 = 8 r 2. The whole answer: 185 r 3.

items.q: Amelia uses short division for 797 ÷ 6. First, 7 ÷ 6 = 1 r 1. What does she divide next?
items.e: 7 ÷ 6 = 1 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 hundred, which is 10 tens. Write it as a small 1 in front of the 9, so you divide 19 next: 19 ÷ 6 = 3 r 1. The whole answer: 132 r 5.

items.q: Ava works out 48 ÷ 3 = 12 r 2. What mistake did she make?
c: She divided by the wrong number
She did not carry the remainders
She missed a 0 in the answer
items.e: Ava divided each digit on its own and threw the remainders away. Each remainder must be carried to the next digit. 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Answer: 16. Check: 16 × 3 = 48.

items.q: Use short division to work out 765 ÷ 9.
items.e: 9 does not go into 7, so carry the 7 to make 76; 76 ÷ 9 = 8 r 4, carry the 4 to make 45; 45 ÷ 9 = 5. Answer: 85. Check: 85 × 9 = 765.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 9 ÷ 4 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 4 = 4. Answer: 24. Check: 24 × 4 = 96.

items.q: Use short division to work out 996 ÷ 6.
items.e: 9 ÷ 6 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 39; 39 ÷ 6 = 6 r 3, carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Answer: 166. Check: 166 × 6 = 996.

items.q: Use short division to work out 904 ÷ 4.
items.e: 9 ÷ 4 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 10; 10 ÷ 4 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Answer: 226. Check: 226 × 4 = 904.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 6 ÷ 3 = 2; 3 does not go into 2, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 3 = 7. Answer: 207. Check: 207 × 3 = 621.

c: She missed a 0 in the answer
She divided by the wrong number
She did not carry the remainders
items.e: Freya divided each digit on its own and threw the remainders away. Each remainder must be carried to the next digit. 7 ÷ 6 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 6 = 1 r 5, carry the 5 to make 54; 54 ÷ 6 = 9. Answer: 119. Check: 119 × 6 = 714.

items.q: Use short division to work out 931 ÷ 7.
items.e: 9 ÷ 7 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 23; 23 ÷ 7 = 3 r 2, carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 7 = 3. Answer: 133. Check: 133 × 7 = 931.

items.q: Use short division to work out 56 ÷ 4.
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 4 = 4. Answer: 14. Check: 14 × 4 = 56.

items.e: 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1. The remainder 1 is 1 hundred, which is 10 tens. Write it as a small 1 in front of the 2, so you divide 12 next: 12 ÷ 3 = 4. The whole answer: 140 r 1.

items.q: Use short division.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 38; 38 ÷ 4 = 9 r 2, carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 4 = 7. Answer: 197. Check: 197 × 4 = 788.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 4 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 4 = 3 r 3, carry the 3 to make 32; 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Answer: 38. Check: 38 × 4 = 152.

items.q: 276 ÷ 4 = 69. Which calculation checks this answer?

c: He did not carry the remainders
He missed a 0 in the answer
items.e: A remainder must be less than the divisor. 4 is more than 3, so 3 goes in once more: 4 − 3 = 1. The answer is 97 r 1. Check: 97 × 3 + 1 = 292.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 13; 13 ÷ 4 = 3 r 1, carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 4 = 4 r 3. Answer: 134 r 3. Check: 134 × 4 + 3 = 539.

items.q: Use short division to work out 705 ÷ 6.
items.e: 7 ÷ 6 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 10; 10 ÷ 6 = 1 r 4, carry the 4 to make 45; 45 ÷ 6 = 7 r 3. Answer: 117 r 3. Check: 117 × 6 + 3 = 705.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 30; 30 ÷ 4 = 7 r 2, carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 4 = 5 r 1. Answer: 175 r 1. Check: 175 × 4 + 1 = 701.

items.q: Use short division to work out 619 ÷ 5.
items.e: 6 ÷ 5 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 5 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 5 = 3 r 4. Answer: 123 r 4. Check: 123 × 5 + 4 = 619.

items.q: Kai works out 519 ÷ 4 = 128 r 7. What mistake did he make?
c: He did not carry the remainders
He missed a 0 in the answer
items.e: A remainder must be less than the divisor. 7 is more than 4, so 4 goes in once more: 7 − 4 = 3. The answer is 129 r 3. Check: 129 × 4 + 3 = 519.

items.q: Use short division to work out 629 ÷ 5.
items.e: 6 ÷ 5 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 5 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 29; 29 ÷ 5 = 5 r 4. Answer: 125 r 4. Check: 125 × 5 + 4 = 629.

items.q: What is the remainder when 244 is divided by 7?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the answer to the division. 7 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 7 = 3 r 3, carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 7 = 4 r 6. Answer: 34 r 6. Check: 34 × 7 + 6 = 244.

items.q: You divide a number by 6. Which of these could be the remainder?
items.e: A remainder is always less than the divisor. When you divide by 6, the remainder can only be 1 to 5 (or 0). If you have 6 or more left, 6 goes in again.

items.q: Use short division to work out 994 ÷ 6.
items.e: 9 ÷ 6 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 39; 39 ÷ 6 = 6 r 3, carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 6 = 5 r 4. Answer: 165 r 4. Check: 165 × 6 + 4 = 994.

items.q: Use short division to work out 854 ÷ 3.
items.e: 8 ÷ 3 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 25; 25 ÷ 3 = 8 r 1, carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 3 = 4 r 2. Answer: 284 r 2. Check: 284 × 3 + 2 = 854.

items.q: Use short division to work out 886 ÷ 7.
items.e: 8 ÷ 7 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 7 = 2 r 4, carry the 4 to make 46; 46 ÷ 7 = 6 r 4. Answer: 126 r 4. Check: 126 × 7 + 4 = 886.

items.q: What is the remainder when 394 is divided by 8?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the answer to the division. 8 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 39; 39 ÷ 8 = 4 r 7, carry the 7 to make 74; 74 ÷ 8 = 9 r 2. Answer: 49 r 2. Check: 49 × 8 + 2 = 394.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 ÷ 5 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 31; 31 ÷ 5 = 6 r 1, carry the 1 to make 17; 17 ÷ 5 = 3 r 2. Answer: 163 r 2. Check: 163 × 5 + 2 = 817.

items.q: Use short division to work out 262 ÷ 3.
items.e: 3 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 26; 26 ÷ 3 = 8 r 2, carry the 2 to make 22; 22 ÷ 3 = 7 r 1. Answer: 87 r 1. Check: 87 × 3 + 1 = 262.

items.q: You divide a number by 9. Which of these could be the remainder?
items.e: A remainder is always less than the divisor. When you divide by 9, the remainder can only be 1 to 8 (or 0). If you have 9 or more left, 9 goes in again.

items.q: You divide a number by 4. Which of these could be the remainder?
items.e: A remainder is always less than the divisor. When you divide by 4, the remainder can only be 1 to 3 (or 0). If you have 4 or more left, 4 goes in again.

items.q: What is the remainder when 557 is divided by 9?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the answer to the division. 9 does not go into 5, so carry the 5 to make 55; 55 ÷ 9 = 6 r 1, carry the 1 to make 17; 17 ÷ 9 = 1 r 8. Answer: 61 r 8. Check: 61 × 9 + 8 = 557.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 does not go into 4, so carry the 4 to make 43; 43 ÷ 7 = 6 r 1, carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 7 = 2 r 5. Answer: 62 r 5. Check: 62 × 7 + 5 = 439.

items.q: Use short division to work out 866 ÷ 3.
items.e: 8 ÷ 3 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 26; 26 ÷ 3 = 8 r 2, carry the 2 to make 26; 26 ÷ 3 = 8 r 2. Answer: 288 r 2. Check: 288 × 3 + 2 = 866.

sets.title: 4-digit numbers ÷ 1-digit numbers, with zeros in the answer

items.q: Use short division to work out 6,465 ÷ 6.
items.e: 6 ÷ 6 = 1; 6 does not go into 4, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 4 to make 46; 46 ÷ 6 = 7 r 4, carry the 4 to make 45; 45 ÷ 6 = 7 r 3. Answer: 1,077 r 3. Check: 1,077 × 6 + 3 = 6,465.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 does not go into 7, so carry the 7 to make 76; 76 ÷ 8 = 9 r 4, carry the 4 to make 47; 47 ÷ 8 = 5 r 7, carry the 7 to make 79; 79 ÷ 8 = 9 r 7. Answer: 959 r 7. Check: 959 × 8 + 7 = 7,679.

items.q: Use short division to work out 5,103 ÷ 3.
items.e: 5 ÷ 3 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 3 = 7; 3 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the answer; 3 ÷ 3 = 1. Answer: 1,701. Check: 1,701 × 3 = 5,103.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 ÷ 6 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 6 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 20; 20 ÷ 6 = 3 r 2, carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Answer: 1,234. Check: 1,234 × 6 = 7,404.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 1,211 ÷ 6?
items.e: 1,211 is close to 1,200, and 12 ÷ 6 = 2, so 1,200 ÷ 6 = 200. The exact answer is 201 r 5.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 9 ÷ 6 = 1 r 3, carry the 3 to make 39; 39 ÷ 6 = 6 r 3, carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 6 = 5 r 4, carry the 4 to make 48; 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Answer: 1,658. Check: 1,658 × 6 = 9,948.

items.q: Use short division to work out 5,232 ÷ 8.
items.e: 8 does not go into 5, so carry the 5 to make 52; 52 ÷ 8 = 6 r 4, carry the 4 to make 43; 43 ÷ 8 = 5 r 3, carry the 3 to make 32; 32 ÷ 8 = 4. Answer: 654. Check: 654 × 8 = 5,232.

items.q: How many digits will the answer to 7,341 ÷ 8 have (not counting the remainder)?

items.q: Use short division to work out 4,012 ÷ 4.
items.e: 4 ÷ 4 = 1; 4 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the answer; 4 does not go into 1, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Answer: 1,003. Check: 1,003 × 4 = 4,012.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 8 does not go into 4, so carry the 4 to make 46; 46 ÷ 8 = 5 r 6, carry the 6 to make 62; 62 ÷ 8 = 7 r 6, carry the 6 to make 64; 64 ÷ 8 = 8. Answer: 578. Check: 578 × 8 = 4,624.

items.q: Maya works out 4,036 ÷ 4 = 19. What mistake did she make?
c: She did not carry the remainders
She missed a 0 in the answer
items.e: Check: 19 × 4 = 76, not 4,036. When 4 does not go into a digit, write 0 in the answer. 4 ÷ 4 = 1; 4 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the answer; 4 does not go into 3, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Answer: 1,009. Check: 1,009 × 4 = 4,036.

items.q: Leo works out 3,045 ÷ 5 = 69. What mistake did he make?
c: He missed a 0 in the answer
He did not carry the remainders
items.e: Check: 69 × 5 = 345, not 3,045. When 5 does not go into a digit, write 0 in the answer. 5 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 30; 30 ÷ 5 = 6; 5 does not go into 4, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 4 to make 45; 45 ÷ 5 = 9. Answer: 609. Check: 609 × 5 = 3,045.

items.q: Use short division to work out 3,714 ÷ 6.
items.e: 6 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 37; 37 ÷ 6 = 6 r 1, carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 6 = 1 r 5, carry the 5 to make 54; 54 ÷ 6 = 9. Answer: 619. Check: 619 × 6 = 3,714.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 4,208 ÷ 7?

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 6 ÷ 6 = 1; 6 does not go into 4, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 4 to make 44; 44 ÷ 6 = 7 r 2, carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Answer: 1,074. Check: 1,074 × 6 = 6,444.

items.q: Lily works out 8,824 ÷ 8 = 113. What mistake did she make?
c: She did not carry the remainders
She missed a 0 in the answer
items.e: Check: 113 × 8 = 904, not 8,824. When 8 does not go into a digit, write 0 in the answer. 8 ÷ 8 = 1; 8 ÷ 8 = 1; 8 does not go into 2, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 8 = 3. Answer: 1,103. Check: 1,103 × 8 = 8,824.

items.q: Use short division to work out 8,241 ÷ 3.
items.e: 8 ÷ 3 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 22; 22 ÷ 3 = 7 r 1, carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 3 = 4 r 2, carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 3 = 7. Answer: 2,747. Check: 2,747 × 3 = 8,241.

items.q: How many digits will the answer to 7,734 ÷ 7 have (not counting the remainder)?
items.e: 7 is at least 7, so the answer starts in the thousands place. 7,734 ÷ 7 = 1,104 r 6.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 7 does not go into 5, so carry the 5 to make 56; 56 ÷ 7 = 8; 7 does not go into 2, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 7 = 4. Answer: 804. Check: 804 × 7 = 5,628.

sets.title: Remainders in context: round up, round down or a fraction

items.q: 19 cakes are shared equally between 3 tables. How many cakes does each table get? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 19 ÷ 3 = 6 r 1. The 1 left over can be shared too: 1 ÷ 3 = 13. So the answer is 6 13 cakes.

items.q: A teacher has 75 pencils. She puts 6 pencils in each pot. 75 ÷ 6 = 12 r 3. How many pots can she fill?
items.e: 75 ÷ 6 = 12 r 3. The 3 pencils left over are not enough to fill another pot, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 12 pots.

items.q: What is the missing number? ? ÷ 8 = 187 r 7
items.e: Use the inverse. Multiply, then add the remainder: 187 × 8 = 1,496 and 1,496 + 7 = 1,503. Check: 1,503 ÷ 8 = 187 r 7.

items.q: A baker has 123 cupcakes. Each box holds 4 cupcakes. 123 ÷ 4 = 30 r 3. How many boxes can the baker fill?
items.e: 123 ÷ 4 = 30 r 3. The 3 cupcakes left over are not enough to fill another box, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 30 boxes.

items.q: A shop has 158 batteries. It sells them in packs of 4. 158 ÷ 4 = 39 r 2. How many full packs can the shop make?
items.e: 158 ÷ 4 = 39 r 2. The 2 batteries left over are not enough to make another pack, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 39 packs.

items.q: 367 ÷ 7 = 52 r 3. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiply the answer by the divisor, then add the remainder: 52 × 7 = 364 and 364 + 3 = 367.

items.q: What is the missing number? ? ÷ 3 = 152 r 2
items.e: Use the inverse. Multiply, then add the remainder: 152 × 3 = 456 and 456 + 2 = 458. Check: 458 ÷ 3 = 152 r 2.

items.q: A 35 m rope is cut into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 35 ÷ 4 = 8 r 3. The 3 left over can be shared too: 3 ÷ 4 = 34. So the answer is 8 34 m.

items.q: 22 litres of juice are poured equally into 3 jugs. How much juice is in each jug? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 22 ÷ 3 = 7 r 1. The 1 left over can be shared too: 1 ÷ 3 = 13. So the answer is 7 13 litres.

items.q: 115 Scouts are going camping. Each tent sleeps 4 people. 115 ÷ 4 = 28 r 3. How many tents are needed?
items.e: 28 tents hold 28 × 4 = 112 people. 3 people still need a place, so you need 1 more: 29 tents. Round up.

items.q: 478 ÷ 6 = 79 r 4. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiply the answer by the divisor, then add the remainder: 79 × 6 = 474 and 474 + 4 = 478.

items.q: 354 ÷ 3 = 118. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiplication is the inverse of division. 118 × 3 = 354, which matches.

items.q: 222 people want a boat ride on the lake. Each boat trip takes 7 people. 222 ÷ 7 = 31 r 5. How many boat trips are needed?
items.e: 31 trips hold 31 × 7 = 217 people. 5 people still need a place, so you need 1 more: 32 trips. Round up.

items.q: What is the missing number? ? ÷ 5 = 185 r 3
items.e: Use the inverse. Multiply, then add the remainder: 185 × 5 = 925 and 925 + 3 = 928. Check: 928 ÷ 5 = 185 r 3.

items.q: 4 friends share 31 pizzas equally. How much pizza does each friend get? Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 31 ÷ 4 = 7 r 3. The 3 left over can be shared too: 3 ÷ 4 = 34. So the answer is 7 34 pizzas.

items.q: 114 children are going on a school trip. Each minibus holds 8 children. 114 ÷ 8 = 14 r 2. How many minibuses are needed?
items.e: 14 minibuses hold 14 × 8 = 112 children. 2 children still need a place, so you need 1 more: 15 minibuses. Round up.

items.q: 174 guests are coming to a party. Each table seats 8 guests. 174 ÷ 8 = 21 r 6. How many tables are needed?
items.e: 21 tables hold 21 × 8 = 168 guests. 6 guests still need a place, so you need 1 more: 22 tables. Round up.

items.q: 623 ÷ 7 = 89. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiplication is the inverse of division. 89 × 7 = 623, which matches.

items.q: What is the missing number? ? ÷ 4 = 199 r 3
items.e: Use the inverse. Multiply, then add the remainder: 199 × 4 = 796 and 796 + 3 = 799. Check: 799 ÷ 4 = 199 r 3.

items.q: A library has 130 books. Each shelf holds 9 books. 130 ÷ 9 = 14 r 4. How many shelves can be filled?
items.e: 130 ÷ 9 = 14 r 4. The 4 books left over are not enough to fill another shelf, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 14 shelves.

sets.title: Word problems: sharing, grouping and what to do with the remainder

items.q: 348 playing cards are dealt out equally to 7 players. Each player gets as many as possible. How many cards are left over?
items.e: Divide: 7 does not go into 3, so carry the 3 to make 34; 34 ÷ 7 = 4 r 6, carry the 6 to make 68; 68 ÷ 7 = 9 r 5. So 348 ÷ 7 = 49 r 5. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 5 cards.

items.q: 188 people are coming to a school concert. The chairs are put out in rows of 9. How many rows are needed so everyone has a seat?
items.e: Divide: 9 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 9 = 2; 9 does not go into 8, so write 0 in the answer and the remainder is 8. So 188 ÷ 9 = 20 r 8. 20 rows are not enough: 8 people would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so the answer is 21 rows.

items.q: A farm collects 717 eggs. It packs them in boxes of 6. How many boxes does it need for all the eggs?
items.e: Divide: 7 ÷ 6 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 6 = 1 r 5, carry the 5 to make 57; 57 ÷ 6 = 9 r 3. So 717 ÷ 6 = 119 r 3. 119 boxes are not enough: 3 eggs would still need a box. You need 1 more, so the answer is 120 boxes.

items.q: Ruby shares 235 sweets equally into 8 party bags. Each bag gets as many as possible. How many sweets are left over?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 23; 23 ÷ 8 = 2 r 7, carry the 7 to make 75; 75 ÷ 8 = 9 r 3. So 235 ÷ 8 = 29 r 3. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 3 sweets.

items.q: There are 157 children at a netball tournament. Each team needs exactly 7 players. How many full teams can be made?
items.e: Divide: 7 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 7 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 17; 17 ÷ 7 = 2 r 3. So 157 ÷ 7 = 22 r 3. The 3 children left over are not enough to make another team, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 22 teams.

items.q: A school spends £2,807 on 7 new laptops. Each laptop costs the same. How much does one laptop cost?
items.e: Divide: 7 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 7 = 4; 7 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the answer; 7 ÷ 7 = 1. So 2,807 ÷ 7 = 401. The answer is £401. Check: 401 × 7 = 2,807.

items.q: Alfie is making necklaces. Each necklace needs 7 beads. He has 278 beads. How many necklaces can he make?
items.e: Divide: 7 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 7 = 3 r 6, carry the 6 to make 68; 68 ÷ 7 = 9 r 5. So 278 ÷ 7 = 39 r 5. The 5 beads left over are not enough to make another necklace, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 39 necklaces.

items.q: A garden centre has 1,479 bulbs. It packs them in bags of 8 and fills as many bags as it can. How many bulbs are not in a bag?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 8 = 1 r 6, carry the 6 to make 67; 67 ÷ 8 = 8 r 3, carry the 3 to make 39; 39 ÷ 8 = 4 r 7. So 1,479 ÷ 8 = 184 r 7. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 7 bulbs.

items.q: A farm has 1,814 eggs. It packs them in boxes of 6. How many boxes can it fill completely?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 18; 18 ÷ 6 = 3; 6 does not go into 1, so write 0 in the answer and carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 6 = 2 r 2. So 1,814 ÷ 6 = 302 r 2. The 2 eggs left over are not enough to fill another box, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 302 boxes.

items.q: 23 pizzas are shared equally between 8 tables at a party. How much pizza does each table get?
items.e: Divide: 23 ÷ 8 = 2 r 7. The 7 left over can be shared too: 7 ÷ 8 = 78. Each gets 2 78 pizzas.

items.q: Arjun bakes 29 flapjacks. He shares them equally between 3 friends. How many flapjacks does each friend get?
items.e: Divide: 29 ÷ 3 = 9 r 2. The 2 left over can be shared too: 2 ÷ 3 = 23. Each gets 9 23 flapjacks.

items.q: 4 friends win £528 in a raffle. They share the money equally. How much does each friend get?
items.e: Divide: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 4 = 3; 8 ÷ 4 = 2. So 528 ÷ 4 = 132. The answer is £132. Check: 132 × 4 = 528.

items.q: A school orders 1,064 exercise books. They come in packs of 8. How many packs does the school order?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 10; 10 ÷ 8 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 26; 26 ÷ 8 = 3 r 2, carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 8 = 3. So 1,064 ÷ 8 = 133. There is no remainder, so the answer is 133 packs.

items.q: Amelia swims 1,108 m in 4 days. She swims the same distance every day. How far does she swim each day?
items.e: Divide: 4 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 4 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 30; 30 ÷ 4 = 7 r 2, carry the 2 to make 28; 28 ÷ 4 = 7. So 1,108 ÷ 4 = 277. There is no remainder, so the answer is 277 m.

items.q: Aisha has £76. Cinema tickets cost £9 each. How many tickets can she buy?
items.e: Divide: 76 ÷ 9 = 8 r 4. The £4 left over is not enough to buy another ticket, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 8 tickets.

items.q: A book has 375 pages. Ethan reads the same number of pages each day and finishes it in 3 days. How many pages does he read each day?
items.e: Divide: 3 ÷ 3 = 1; 7 ÷ 3 = 2 r 1, carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 3 = 5. So 375 ÷ 3 = 125. There is no remainder, so the answer is 125 pages.

items.q: George is putting 231 photos into an album. Each page holds 4 photos. How many pages does he need?
items.e: Divide: 4 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 23; 23 ÷ 4 = 5 r 3, carry the 3 to make 31; 31 ÷ 4 = 7 r 3. So 231 ÷ 4 = 57 r 3. 57 pages are not enough: 3 photos would still need a page. You need 1 more, so the answer is 58 pages.

items.q: A class raises £576 at a cake sale. The money is shared equally between 4 charities. How much does each charity get?
items.e: Divide: 5 ÷ 4 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 17; 17 ÷ 4 = 4 r 1, carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 4 = 4. So 576 ÷ 4 = 144. The answer is £144. Check: 144 × 4 = 576.

items.q: 205 pupils are going to a museum. Each minibus has 8 seats for pupils. How many minibuses are needed?
items.e: Divide: 8 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 20; 20 ÷ 8 = 2 r 4, carry the 4 to make 45; 45 ÷ 8 = 5 r 5. So 205 ÷ 8 = 25 r 5. 25 minibuses are not enough: 5 pupils would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so the answer is 26 minibuses.

items.q: Poppy runs 1,206 m by running 6 laps of the school field. Each lap is the same length. How long is one lap?
items.e: Divide: 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 6 = 2; 6 does not go into 0, so write 0 in the answer; 6 ÷ 6 = 1. So 1,206 ÷ 6 = 201. There is no remainder, so the answer is 201 m.
